The Ferry Road
written for enough's verse fixtures, terza rima (2026)

We walked the ferry road at end of day,
the river low and slower than the hill,
the gulls already drifting on their way.

The water kept its counsel, flat and still;
a heron stood where reeds were growing back,
and nothing moved the evening but its will.

We crossed the stones that marked the older track,
where carts had worn a hollow in the ground,
and found the boat drawn up and tarred in black.

The ferryman was nowhere to be found;
his lantern hung unlit beside the glass,
and all his rope lay coiled and wrapped around.

We waited till the light began to pass.
